videos.script: Lesson one scored six articles against a question and read the numbers as higher is closer. {{scores}} This lesson opens that number up. A vector is an arrow, with a direction and a length. {{arrow}} Turn every arrow in the space by the same amount, and every score stays exactly where it was. So no single number in a vector means anything on its own. {{rotate}} You will compute a dot product by hand, with three numbers on paper. Then you will double one vector and watch the score double with it. {{double}} Cosine similarity divides the length out and keeps only the angle. {{angle}} Distance measures the straight line between two points. For vectors of length one, it ranks exactly like the cosine. {{distance}} Then you will meet a model that does not normalise its vectors. It puts the wrong article first, because one arrow is longer than another. {{length}} Last, you will score every pair of a hundred and fifty customer messages. They crowd into a narrow band, and each model's band sits somewhere else. {{band}} By the end, a score will mean something precise, for one model and one collection, and nothing outside them. {{end}}
